Utility Functions Module

This module provides utility functions and configuration management
for the F1Brainz system.

Key components:
    - config: Configuration management with YAML validation
    - constants: Centralized constants (calendars, thresholds, etc.)
    - ids: Driver ID mapping between FastF1 and Ergast

Example:
    from src.utils.config import Config
    from src.utils.constants import F1_CALENDARS

    config = Config.load_config()
    seasons = Config.get_seasons()
    calendar = F1_CALENDARS[2024]

Console encoding helpers for CLI script entrypoints.

On Windows a redirected stdout/stderr defaults to the cp1252 code page, so a plain
``print("→")`` raises ``UnicodeEncodeError`` and crashes the run. Scripts that emit
non-ASCII status output call :func:`force_utf8_console` at the top of ``main`` so
their output is safe regardless of the active code page (see issue #358).

Shared, F1-agnostic resource-utilization policy core.

This module decides *how hard the machine is pushed* without ever changing *what is
computed*. It maps a coarse utilization level to a concrete worker/thread/priority
plan and runs a list of jobs through that plan — either in a process pool or, at one
worker, in a plain in-process loop.

Determinism contract (load-bearing for every caller):
  * `run_jobs` always returns results in **input order**, byte-identical regardless of
    `n_workers`, because results are reassembled by their submission index.
  * `n_workers == 1` short-circuits to a sequential in-process loop — no pool, no
    pickling — so it reproduces the plain sequential path exactly.

The module is intentionally free of any F1/domain concepts (no DB, calendar, or evo
imports) and holds no mutable module-level state. It must import cleanly even when
`torch` is not installed; the torch import lives inside `init_worker` and is guarded.

GATING validation harness for #662 G6 (epic #659): the substantive falsification.

Computes the two GATING checks the g6-handoff.md defines, against REAL 2023 data:

GATING-1 (claim:map-stable)
    Cross-weekend stability is a SCOPED NULL for 2023 -- F1 runs each circuit once
    per season, so there is no second same-circuit weekend to compare (see
    ``scoped_null_2023_no_repeat_circuits``). The substantive PROXY is split-half
    within-weekend stability: derive the tiling from two DISJOINT driver-subset
    halves of the same weekend's field and compare boundary distances
    (``split_half_boundary_drift``). The MEDIAN drift is the asserted gate
    (< ``MAP_STABILITY_DRIFT_M``, imported); the MAX is reported, never asserted --
    it is dominated by the noisier p10 braking-onset quantile over a half-sized
    subsample (see this module's own README-style notes below), not tiling
    instability at the geometry level.

GATING-2 (claim:typing-correct)
    Physical-corner spot-checks against real ground truth: Bahrain's PHYSICAL
    corner count + apex locations vs the P4 excursion's independent count
    (``.agent-work/archive/2026-07-25-explore-ref-utilization/excursions/P4-RESULT.md``),
    and a 2nd circuit's physical corner count vs its known official turn count.

    "Physical corner" merges contiguous CORNER segments -- this ALREADY absorbs a
    sector-split corner (two adjacent CORNER rows straddling an FIA sector line):
    ``sector_nesting.nest_sectors``'s split-not-snap duplicates the SAME seg_type
    on both sides of a sector cut, so a split corner is still two ADJACENT
    same-type segments in the final (nested) ``seg_type_code`` array -- no
    sector-line-aware special case is needed beyond ordinary contiguous-run
    grouping.

Construction vs gating (review T3): tiling-completeness (G2) and sector-nesting
exactness (G3) are CONSTRUCTION checks, already exercised in their own test
suites -- they catch coverage/arithmetic bugs (gaps, overlaps, a sector line
landing outside the lap), never mis-typing. GATING-1/GATING-2 here are the
checks that can falsify an unstable or physically-wrong map.

No-frame-kill: every check either produces a real number from real data, or
reports a clean, explicit scoped-null / skip reason -- never a fabricated
number and never a silently-fudged fallback.

Usage
-----
    python scripts/validate_segment_map_662.py

Practice Preprocessor for the Evolutionary Predictor.

Extracts rich, time-based features from FP/Sprint practice session lap data,
replacing position-only features with sector-level performance metrics.

Features computed per driver:
- 6x raw sector features: lr_best, lr_expected, lr_variation, qs_best, qs_expected, qs_variation
- 6x compound-adjusted sector features: same metrics with tire compound normalization
- representative-lap raw bundles for LR/QS in raw and adjusted space
- 2x teammate gap: gap to teammate in long run and quali sim configs
- 1x clean lap count: preparation/reliability proxy
- 1x FP progression: improvement from FP1 to final practice session

Environment features per race:
- air_density: estimated from altitude + temperature + humidity
- avg_track_temp, avg_air_temp, avg_humidity

Structural Clean Lap Criteria:
- valid_lap = 1
- No pit in/out times (full flying lap)
- All three sector times present

Bucket Pace Gates:
- Short run laps within 108% of session's fastest structural-clean lap
- Long run laps within 110% of session's fastest structural-clean lap

Stint Classification:
- Long run: > QUALI_SIM_MAX_LAPS consecutive clean laps in a stint
- Quali sim: 1-QUALI_SIM_MAX_LAPS consecutive clean laps

Normalization (median-relative gap-to-median; the sole encoding):
- Pace-LEVEL features: (value - field_median) / field_median; faster-than-median ->
  negative, slower -> positive. Higher-is-better levels flip the sign so better -> negative.
- Variation / dispersions: value / field_median_lap_time (uncentered magnitude;
  "spread as a fraction of a lap").
- Missing / degenerate (median <= 0) fallback: 0.0 (median-neutral); the per-feature
  _missing indicator carries the absence.

Per-race scoring + execution helpers for :mod:`sampled_backtest`.

Split out of ``sampled_backtest.py`` to keep that file within the simplification
file-size limit. This module holds the pure per-race scorer ``_score_one_race`` (the
behavior-preservation core of the sampled backtest), its private sub-helpers, and the
two execution strategies — in-process sequential and the opt-in ``run_jobs`` parallel
path with its module-level, spawn-safe worker. Nothing here mutates module-level state.

``sampled_backtest.backtest_sampled_runtime`` imports the two ``_score_races_*`` drivers
lazily (inside the function) to avoid an import cycle: this module imports scoring
primitives from ``sampled_backtest`` at load time, so the reverse edge must be deferred.

Real per-period cutoff pipeline for the walk-forward backtest (#439).

This is the heavy path P1-P3 use (and that the G4 run executes). It automates the
``docs/evo/analysis_refresh.md`` recipe with the in-season as-of cutoff, fully isolated
under a per-period work area so it never touches the committed ``params/gold`` artifacts:

  1. Assemble a per-period ``compound_prior_root`` containing the train-year priors (2018-2024)
     copied from gold. Compound priors are CROSS-SEASON throughout: ``allow_same_season_compound_prior``
     is ``false``, matching the promoted gold's compound handling. This is leakage-safe (zero 2025
     compound data) and avoids the 2018 same-season prior's missing beta_C1/beta_C2 entries.
  2. Write a research-mode gold-cycle TOML with ``eval_year_train_through_round=N`` /
     ``eval_round_range=[N+1, N+6]``, anchor + quali_pace_gap to match promoted gold, and
     isolated output/report/calibration dirs.
  3. Run the gold cycle, then static fusion -> assemble period-local trained manifest ->
     trained sampled-runtime comparison (runbook Steps 3/3b/4) restricted to the period's
     rounds. The comparison is given EXPLICIT period manifests so it scores this period's
     cutoff-trained model, not the global promoted gold. The global ``materialize`` step is
     skipped (it targets committed reports/evo + params/gold and needs gold/fusion timestamp
     equality); the trained manifest's absolute period-local module paths load directly.
  4. Collect each eval round's predicted finishing-position distribution from the trained
     comparison result.

The path/config construction is pure and unit-tested; the subprocess steps live in
:class:`SubprocessPipeline`, which is exercised by the real run (never in unit tests — the
multi-hour calls are mocked there via the orchestrator's :class:`PipelinePort`).

Batch driver for the per-session physics fit store (Epic 2 P0, #492).

Residual builder + ephemeris batch (#509 Step 2, Task 5 -- THE DELIVERABLE)
per docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-05-ideal-lap-generator-ephemeris-design.md
Sec. "Residuals are the deliverable".

For each clean race lap of each driver at each (year, gp): compute the lap's
state (compound + tyre_age from ``lap_times``, mass via ``mass_model.
race_mass``) -> ``ideal_lap`` at that state -> ``residual_s = observed_lap_s -
ideal_lap_s`` -> collect ``eph_state``/``eph_residual`` rows -> ``write_run``.
The residual distribution IS the steering instrument (low = trusted state,
high = where to push next) and, at a fixed car state, the driver signal.

## Scope (ratified, see design doc's Open decision 4)

Race sessions only, for circuits the wear model has measured -- that
validates the wear join against real in-session degradation. Q/FP are a
follow-on (Q has no in-session wear to validate against; FP's compound
offsets still need the push-lap filter, tracked separately as issue #16).
``ideal_lap`` itself is still called with ``session_type="Q"`` per lap --
the car-capability anchor (fit row + ribbon geometry) is the Q-session
ceiling; only the STATE (compound, tyre_age, fuel_mass) being evaluated at
comes from the race lap.

## Caching within one (year, gp, driver): the one deliberate optimization

``ideal_lap`` documents its ``fit_row``/``ribbon`` parameters as "injection
seams for offline testing" -- they are equally valid as a real caching seam,
and this builder needs it: a race stint is dozens of laps, and ``ideal_lap``
would otherwise reload the Q session and rebuild ribbon geometry from
scratch on EVERY lap. Per driver, this builder resolves the fit row (via
``_load_ok_fits``, one query for the whole gp), the ribbon
(``generator._build_ribbon``), and -- critically -- the power curve
(``generator._power_curve_from_row``) exactly ONCE, then reuses all three
across every clean lap of that driver's race. The power-curve resolution
matters most: a fit row written before Task 1 has ``power_curve=None``, and
``ideal_lap`` treats a miss as "re-fit the whole session" -- paying that cost
on every lap of a stint (instead of once) turns an O(drivers) batch into an
O(drivers x laps) one. Baking the resolved curve back into a copy of the row
before the per-lap loop keeps ``ideal_lap``'s own cheap path (``row.get(
"power_curve") is not None``) live for every subsequent lap.

## Terrain / banking (Task 11)

``_build_terrain`` resolves ONE pooled terrain profile per (year, gp) --
banking is a circuit property, not a per-driver/per-lap one -- and every
``ideal_lap``/``ideal_lap_sigma_grid`` call this gp is threaded the SAME
``terrain`` object (see ``generator._track_df_from_ribbon``'s position-joined
``bank_rad`` column). A session/profile build failure degrades to
``terrain=None`` (logged once here, never fatal) -- every downstream call
then reproduces the pre-Task-11 flat-track simulation exactly.

## Robustness (mirrors src.physics.wear.batch / sweep.sweep_event)

A bad (year, gp), a driver with no ok Q fit, a driver whose ribbon/power-curve
setup fails, or a single lap whose ``ideal_lap`` call raises are all SKIPPED
(logged, not fatal) -- never abort the whole batch. A lap whose ideal can't be
built gets no residual row: nothing is fabricated.

## Capability vs realized kappa (Task 6, capability-wear-model-v2)

``kappa_for_corner`` (called with the SAME hardcoded ``{"label": "traction"}``
fingerprint the pre-existing ``kappa_lat``/``kappa_long`` state fields already
use) is called TWICE per lap when ``wear_model`` is present: once at its
default ``channel="capability"`` (the value that ``ideal_lap``'s own ceiling
derates against -- Task 5's default, unchanged here) and once explicitly with
``channel="realized"``, for the identical ``(circuit, compound)``. Both calls
return ``(kappa_lat, kappa_long)`` -- BOTH axes are stored (``kappa_cap_lat``/
``kappa_cap_long``/``kappa_realized_lat``/``kappa_realized_long``), not the
longitudinal axis alone: lateral (apex) is the PRIMARY wear signal the panel
actually fits on, longitudinal (traction-exit) is secondary, and the ideal's
own ceiling derates both -- dropping either would under-represent the
driver's management (a Task-6-review correction; an initial build stored
longitudinal only).

``mgmt_discount_{lat,long} = kappa_cap_{lat,long} - kappa_realized_{lat,long}``
-- positive when the driver managed that axis's tyre wear (realized came in
below what pushing flat out would have cost), ~zero when the stint was run
flat out. NOTE this is capability MINUS realized, not the design doc Sec. 6's
literal "realized - capability" phrasing -- that phrasing is a transposition;
the design doc's own worked example (managed stint -> discount > 0) only
holds under this sign, confirmed on Task-6 review.

``kappa_for_corner`` keys purely on ``(circuit, compound)`` -- no lap/tyre-age
dependence -- so every one of these six values is already constant across
every lap of one stint (same circuit, same compound throughout). Computing
them inside the existing per-lap loop is therefore equivalent to the
ratified per-stint granularity (design doc Open decision 3), not a weaker
per-lap approximation of it -- no separate per-stint aggregation pass is
needed.

## source_versions_json (the reproducibility pin)

Per the design doc's ``eph_runs`` schema, ``source_versions_json`` must pin
what this ephemeris was built from. ``wear_model_run_id`` is a real pinned
value -- ordinarily ``wear.store.latest_run``, resolved ONCE and held fixed
for the whole build (every lap in this run derates against the SAME wear
run, not whatever ``latest_run`` would independently resolve to per-call);
when ``wear_db_path`` doesn't exist on disk at all, ``latest_run`` is never
called (it would auto-vivify an empty file there), ``load_model``'s own
Task-12 snapshot fallback resolves the model instead, and
``wear_model_run_id`` pins that snapshot's run via
``wear.store.latest_snapshot_run_id`` -- still the run actually loaded, just
not a db row.
``fit_store_build`` is the sorted set of distinct ``engine_sha`` values across
every fit row this run consumed -- a real per-row provenance field FitStore
already carries. ``mass_model_version``/``smoother_version`` (Task 7/9) now pin REAL
module constants -- ``mass_model.MODEL_VERSION`` (the fuel/mass + mass-sigma
law) and ``trajectory.SMOOTHER_VERSION`` (the PVAT smoother's Matern order +
calibration scheme); both were honest "no constant yet" placeholders before
Tasks 7/9 added those constants (the design doc's Open decision 1 gap, now
closed).
``wear_model_push_quantile`` (Task 6, capability-wear-model-v2) is the push
threshold (``wear.batch.run_batch``'s ``push_quantile`` param) the pinned
``wear_model_run_id`` was built with -- read via ``_wear_push_quantile``, a
raw query on that run's own ``wear_runs.params_json`` (``WearModel`` doesn't
carry it). ``None`` for a realized-only/legacy wear model or no wear model at
all -- the wear-model VERSION itself needs no separate field here, since
``wear_model_run_id`` already pins it (a versioned-artifact run_id IS the
version).

Season batch driver for the five-view estimate store (#496/#492).

For each season x GP: load the quali ONCE, group the session's drivers by
constructor, run the #496 cross-view estimator on each constructor's car pair
(with the #498 refinement optionally feeding the views), and upsert the
per-constructor ``SessionEstimate``. Idempotent (skip stored rows unless force)
and crash-tolerant (a missing session or a failing constructor is recorded, never
fatal). The ``*_fn`` seams let tests inject fakes without the FastF1 cache.

Season batch driver for the grip-baseline store (module G, issue #663).

Mirrors ``estimate_batch.py``'s injectable-collaborator-fn pattern: for each
season -> GP (from an injectable ``calendar_fn``) -> session type (every type
in ``src.utils.constants.SESSION_TYPES`` when ``session_type`` is
``None``, else just the one given -- matching g2's
``decision:session-scope-uniform``, which generalized the fit itself to any
session type), skip if already stored unless ``force``, call the injected
``fit_fn`` (g2's real per-session fit by default) and upsert whatever it
returns.

Unlike ``estimate_batch.py`` (which estimates a raw view object and needs a
separate ``record_fn`` to turn it into a storable record), g2's ``fit_fn``
IS the record producer -- ``fit_session_grip_baseline`` already returns a
fully-populated ``GripEstimateRecord`` (``fit_status`` in
``{"ok", "thin_fallback", "error"}``) or ``None`` when the session is absent
from the DB. So here ``record_fn`` covers the one remaining gap: building an
error record for a session whose ``fit_fn`` call RAISES outright (e.g. a
DB-connection failure before g1's own internal ``error_record`` path could
run) -- it defaults to ``grip_store.error_record``, the same never-lose-a-
failure convention g1's store already implements. This is a deliberate
re-mapping of the seam's role for grip's single-function fit shape, not a
literal copy of ``estimate_batch.py``'s split -- see g3's IMPLEMENTER_RESULT
assumptions.

A session missing from the DB (``fit_fn`` returns ``None``) is counted
(``sessions_missing``), never fatal. A session whose ``fit_fn`` call raises
is caught, converted to an error record via ``record_fn``, upserted, and the
batch continues -- one bad session must never sink the whole run.

Race session data loader — pure data adapter for race stints (#563 g2).

Produces ``RaceStintData`` objects (one per qualifying stint) consumed by the
g3 stint estimator.  No view fitting, no decay model — this is a data-loading
seam that sits between the SQLite ``lap_times`` table, the ``TelemetryStore``
(Parquet telemetry), and the physics fit chain.

Design constraints (all DECIDED, do not change without flagging):
  - ``track_status`` from ``lap_times`` must ALWAYS reach ``race_mass(...)``.
    Passing ``track_statuses=None`` silently is a hard gate violation.
  - ``tyre_life`` is the ABSOLUTE value from ``lap_times.tyre_life``.
    Do NOT subtract the per-stint minimum or normalize.
    VER Bahrain 2023 stint 1 starts at tyre_life=4 (FastF1 installation-lap
    accounting); the consumer decides how to interpret the offset.
  - ``n_race_laps = max(lap_number)`` across ALL drivers in the session.
  - No imports from src/evo_predictor, src/latent_power, src/compound_prior.
  - No direct FastF1 calls; all data from SQLite (lap_times) + TelemetryStore.

Clean-lap definition (g2 gate):
  ``valid_lap=1 AND pit_in_time IS NULL AND pit_out_time IS NULL
   AND track_status='1'``

Qualifying stint = one distinct ``stint_id`` in ``lap_times``.

Session-type seam (#575 Phase-A task 1):
  ``load_race_stints`` (and ``_get_session_id``) take a ``session_type``
  parameter (default ``'R'``) selecting which SQLite session and
  TelemetryStore payload to load: ``'R'`` (race), ``'S'`` (sprint), ``'Q'``
  (qualifying), ``'SQ'`` (sprint qualifying). Q/SQ use a constant quali-trim
  mass (``mass_model.quali_mass``) instead of the race burn-down model,
  since those are short low-fuel runs; R/S use ``race_mass`` with the
  session's own lap count (see ``_lap_masses``). The ``track_statuses``
  hard gate above still binds for R/S.

HP-calibration fallback for practice sessions (FP follow-on to #575 Phase-A):
  When a driver's own-session smoother-HP calibration fails (fragmented FP
  running starves the calibration window; see ``_hp_fallback``), a same-
  weekend HP is borrowed (own race session -> own other practice session ->
  pooled median of other drivers in the same session) rather than dropping
  the driver outright.  Gated strictly to ``session_type != 'R'`` -- the race
  path is untouched and returns ``{}`` exactly as before when native
  calibration fails.

Trust-profile PVAT gate (#3, D9 "WIRE" verdict on grading.py):
  Whenever ``pvat_db`` is active, each fitted lap's quality is scored via
  ``grading.compute_trust_profile`` (held-out chi^2 + NIS summary over the
  SAME padded window the lap was fit on) and logged. The opt-in
  ``max_trust_chi2`` argument additionally SKIPS the PVAT write (not the
  fit itself) for a lap whose held-out chi^2 exceeds it. Default
  ``max_trust_chi2=None`` is log-only -- every fitted lap is still
  persisted, matching pre-#3 behaviour.
  COST: +~33% per lap on the pvat_db path only (one extra held-out
  StintSmoother refit over the lap+overhang window, on top of the 3
  refits fit_lap's own bootstrap already pays) -- never paid when
  pvat_db is None.
  FAIL-OPEN: a scoring failure is logged and never gates or blocks the
  write -- the lap persists with NULL trust_* columns. See
  ``_score_and_persist_pvat``/``load_race_stints``'s ``max_trust_chi2``
  docstring for the full contract.

Configuration for the physics parameter estimator.

This module defines the PhysicsEstimatorConfig dataclass that holds all
tuning parameters for the physics-based parameter estimation pipeline.

Offline single-quali-session fit → FitRecord / SessionFitFull (Epic 2 P0/P1, #492).

Lifts the validated smoother→adapter→estimator chain from
``scripts/plot_capability_diagnostics.py::fit_session`` (the #488 production
path) with two deltas: it operates on a PRELOADED session (load once, loop
drivers) and loads ``weather=True`` so air density is the real measured value.

Public entry points
-------------------
fit_driver(session, driver, ...) -> FitRecord
    Batch path: fit one driver, return a flat FitRecord for the store.

fit_session_full(session, driver, ...) -> SessionFitFull | None
    Diagnostic path: re-fit one driver and return params + best-lap geometry
    (distance/speed arrays).  Used by ``sim_evaluator.evaluate_session`` as
    its re-fit fallback and, as a DB-first-on-miss fallback, by
    ``ideal_lap.generator`` (#575 Task 3). The fit store DOES now persist the
    power curve (theta_P_times/theta_P_values/theta_P_covariance, as
    ``FitRecord.power_curve`` — #575 Task 1), and ``fit_store.
    params_from_record`` reconstructs the full params from a row without
    this re-fit; ``ideal_lap.generator`` reads the stored power curve
    DB-first and only falls back to this re-fit path when a row predates
    Task 1.

fit_best_lap_trace(session, driver, ...) -> (best_distance, best_speed_real, best_lap_s) | None
    Cheap subset of ``fit_session_full`` used by ``sim_evaluator``'s
    store-hit path (#575 follow-on, sim-evaluator wiring): when ``params``
    itself comes from ``fit_store.params_from_record`` instead of a re-fit,
    this recovers ONLY the real best-lap trace (never persisted by
    ``FitStore``) via HP calibration + a single ``fit_lap`` call on the
    fastest lap — skipping every other flying lap's smoothing and
    ``ParameterEstimator.estimate_parameters`` entirely.

Canonical batch path: sweep -> fingerprint -> panel -> season model ->
versioned store, per
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-04-wear-model-productization-design.md
Sec. "Canonical path".

    py -m src.physics.wear.batch --years 2022 2023 2024 2025 2026

Per year: fingerprint_year, then panel_year for both phases (v_apex ->
lateral axis, v_out -> longitudinal axis), restricted to whichever GPs
fingerprint_year actually found data for (NOT the caller's raw ``gps``
argument -- panel_year has no missing-file guard of its own, so feeding it
an unresolved "all" or a GP list with holes would crash the batch; deriving
year_gps from fingerprint_year's own return frame is the safe intersection).
Across years: season_model.load_year_axis + rubber_map + is_wet assemble
each axis's wet-excluded season cells table (the same join
``scripts/wear_season_table.py`` did pre-promotion), season_model.fit_axis
fits S x R + covariance per axis, and the two axes are bundled into one
``store.WearModel`` and written via ``store.write_run``.

Per-event sweep is OFF by default (``skip_sweep=True``): the per-(year, gp)
laps/slopes/resets/windows CSVs are the regenerable cache Task 1 built, and
re-sweeping is expensive (telemetry-store reads); ``--sweep-missing`` opts
in. ``sweep.sweep_event`` takes an explicit ``data_dir`` (Task 6 seam --
resolves to ``sweep._DATA_DIR`` at call time when omitted), and
``_sweep_missing`` forwards this batch's own ``data_dir`` through, so
``--sweep-missing`` targets whichever ``data_dir`` the batch was invoked
with, not just the real data directory; it is still not exercised by the
offline test suite (the default ``skip_sweep=True`` path never reaches it).

layer1_physics.py -- Layer 1 of the four-layer weekend-state model (#626 g2).

Layer 1 is the "explained-physics" layer: it removes a **density** (from the
g1 frame's MEASURED-pressure ``rho`` column) and **mass/fuel**
(``mass_kg_assumed``) component from each of the 11 axis estimates, leaving a
per car-weekend x axis ``explained`` value, a ``residual`` (``axis -
explained``), and an honest propagated ``sigma`` for that residual.

Why this is NOT "divide by rho" on a raw force
------------------------------------------------
The 11 axes (``frame.AXES``) are already-fit CAPABILITY estimates
(``drag_area_closed_m2`` is a CdA in m^2, ``max_power_w`` a power in W, ...)
and the upstream estimator (``src/physics/layer2/session_fit.py`` via
``_density_from_session``) already used the session's own MEASURED rho when
fitting them -- so a naive "F = 0.5*rho*v^2*CdA" correction on top would be
double-applying physics the estimator already applied.  What Layer 1 models
instead is the RESIDUAL density/mass leakage that survives into an
already-density-normalized capability estimate: e.g. an assumed-mass error
propagates almost linearly into a force/power-derived coefficient like CdA or
P_max (because those are recovered via F = m*a with an ASSUMED m), while a
directly-measured acceleration (braking/traction/lateral) does not carry that
leakage to first order.  This is exactly the split
``src/physics/layer2/systematic_budget.py`` already draws per-session in
production (cda/p_max carry a mass+rho systematic; the braking/traction frontier
does not to first order, because "mass/rho cancel in the de-conflation" for
A0/A2 and the frontier's own fit sigma already dwarfs its <2.5% systematic).
[#627/#506 retired the static ``estimate_store.SYSTEMATIC_FLOOR`` in favour of
the per-session ``systematic_budget`` shared/session-varying split.]  Layer 1 extends that SAME physical split to the 11 axes,
including the 3 "aero-slope" companions (``brake_aero_decel_per_m``,
``traction_aero_accel_per_m``, ``lateral_aero_grip_g``) where density enters
directly through their own 0.5*rho*v^2 term, and leaves the remaining 4
purely-mechanical acceleration axes (``brake_decel_ms2``,
``traction_accel_ms2``, ``lateral_mech_grip_g``, ``coast_rolling_decel_ms2``)
as an honest, code-enforced NO-OP (explained == 0, residual == raw value) --
see ``DENSITY_SENSITIVE_AXES`` / ``MASS_SENSITIVE_AXES`` below.

Density input
--------------
``rho`` is the g1 frame's store column -- itself computed upstream from a
session's MEASURED barometric pressure via
``src.utils.environment.moist_air_density_from_pressure`` (see
``tests/unit/physics/weekend_state/test_layer1_physics.py::test_rho_matches_measured_pressure``
for the bit-for-bit reproduction against the raw telemetry store).  Layer 1
compares densities in LOG-space throughout (density is multiplicative), and
its reference density ``RHO_REF_KG_M3`` is derived from the SAME measured-
pressure formula applied to the ISA standard atmosphere (15C, 0% humidity,
101325 Pa) -- never a bare hardcoded ``1.2``.

Mass input and an honest identification limit
-----------------------------------------------
``mass_kg_assumed`` in the g1 frame is CONSTANT within a season (it tracks
the year's minimum-weight regulation, not per-race fuel load -- verified:
every (year) group has exactly one distinct value).  That means the mass
term:

  * CANNOT be estimated from within-car-season data (zero within-season
    variance to regress against) -- attempting a between-year fit would
    mostly capture regulation-era performance shifts (e.g. the 2022 ground-
    effect reset), not a clean mass-physics effect.  So the per-axis mass
    SENSITIVITY (``MASS_ELASTICITY``) is assigned from first-principles
    units reasoning (F = m*a: force/power-derived axes carry ~unit
    elasticity to an assumed-mass error; already-per-unit-mass acceleration
    axes carry none), not fit from this store.
  * Contributes ZERO net effect to any same-year comparison (e.g. the
    Mexico<->Monaco falsifiable check below): both venues share the same
    year's ``mass_kg_assumed``, so the mass term cancels identically in the
    residual gap.  It only matters for cross-year comparisons, which this
    layer does not otherwise make.

This is reported honestly rather than manufactured: the mass component here
is real (grounded in the same F=ma reasoning ``estimate_store.py`` cites for
"p_max: mass-dominated"), but its measurable effect on this store is small
and, for same-season comparisons, exactly zero.

Falsifiable Mexico<->Monaco check
------------------------------------
``mexico_monaco_residual_consistency`` compares the SAME constructor's
Layer-1 residual at Mexico (rho ~0.90-0.92) vs Monaco (rho ~1.16-1.20, a
~24% density gap) across every shared car-season in the store.  Mexico and
Monaco differ in aero trim and track character too (a genuine setup
confound, not just density) -- so the assertion this module supports is a
CONSISTENCY-IMPROVEMENT claim (the corrected residual gap is measurably
smaller, in propagated-sigma units, than the raw/density-ignored gap), not a
claim of exact closure to <1 sigma on every car-season.
